mainTopic: End of פרק ראשית הגז, the opening משנה of פרק שילוח הקן, and the גמרא on its phrases and on the exemption of sacrificial birds
overview: The amud opens by finishing פרק ראשית הגז. From an earlier case the גמרא learns that people do not sell the כהן's gifts. So if the seller kept some wool, he gives ראשית הגז; if he kept none, the buyer gives it. After the הדרן, פרק שילוח הקן begins. Its משנה says the מצוה applies everywhere and at all times, but only to non-sacred, kosher birds that are not מזומן. It compares this to כסוי הדם and ends with a מחלוקת about a male קורא. In the גמרא, רבי אבין and רבי מיישא explain when the משנה's phrases 'בארץ ובחוצה לארץ', 'בפני הבית ושלא בפני הבית' and 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' are needed. They also defend the גיד הנשה case with the idea of איידי. Then the גמרא learns from the פסוק 'שלח תשלח את האם' why sacrificial birds are exempt. רבינא extends this to a kosher bird that killed a person. The גמרא begins asking what exact case רבינא means, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person does not sell the priest's gifts
steps.stepSummary: From the earlier case, the גמרא draws a general principle: people do not sell the gifts that belong to the כהן. It applies the same principle to ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that a person does not sell the כהן's gifts. Here too, with the first shearing, a person does not sell the כהן's gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof. It takes the rule learned from the case just before (selling an animal's innards) and says the same rule works for wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the כהן's gifts were not part of the sale unless they were sold by weight. The גמרא learns from this that people simply do not sell the כהן's share. Now it says ראשית הגז works the same way, which sets up the practical ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / evidently: a conclusion drawn from a source
The gifts that belong to the כהן
Here too: applying the same rule to a new case

phrases.english: Evidently, the gifts of the priest —
a person does not sell.
Here too, the gifts of the priest —
phrases.notes: "Here" means ראשית הגז, the first shearing of wool.

phrases.english: a person does not sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מַתָּנוֹת דְּכֹהֵן לָא מְזַבֵּין אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from the earlier case on the daf, before this section begins.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן's gifts are not included when someone sells wool.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier case of selling an animal's innards, where the gifts were not part of the sale.

steps.title: Who gives the first shearing when wool is sold
steps.stepSummary: If the seller kept some wool, the seller must give ראשית הגז. If he kept none, the buyer must give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: if the seller kept some wool, the seller is obligated, because the buyer tells him, 'The כהן's gift is with you.' If he kept none, the buyer is obligated, because the seller tells him, 'I did not sell you the כהן's gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the practical ruling that comes out of the principle in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כהן's share is never really sold, the question is only who should hand it over. If the seller still has wool, the buyer can say the gift is sitting with the seller. If the seller has no wool left, the obligation falls on the buyer, and the seller can say he never sold him the כהן's share in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Left over / kept some for himself

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן's gifts are not part of a sale. If the seller kept some wool, he gives ראשית הגז. If he kept none, the buyer gives it.

phrases.english: Therefore: if the seller left some over —
the seller is obligated,
for the buyer can say to him:
"The priest's gift is with you."
If he did not leave any over — the buyer is obligated,
for the seller can say to him:
"I did not sell you the priest's gift."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 1 to decide the practical law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Seller kept wool means the seller gives ראשית הגז. Seller kept none means the buyer gives it.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing line of the chapter ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter ראשית הגז. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is the traditional farewell said when a chapter is finished. It shows we have reached the end of one unit and a new chapter is about to start.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula for a chapter
The first shearing: the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The First Shearing."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that step 2 completed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter ראשית הגז is finished.

steps.title: Where and when sending away the mother bird applies
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says שילוח הקן applies in ארץ ישראל and outside it, with or without the בית המקדש, to חולין but not to מוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sending away the mother bird applies in the Land and outside the Land, while the Temple stands and when it does not, to non-sacred birds but not to consecrated ones.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה sets out the basic scope of the מצוה of שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives three ranges. The מצוה does not depend on place (ארץ ישראל or outside) or on time (with or without the בית המקדש). Here it sets one limit: the מצוה does not apply to birds that are מוקדשין. More limits come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Sending away the mother bird from the nest
Things dedicated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: Sending away the mother bird from the nest applies
in the Land and outside the Land,
when the Temple stands and when it does not,
to non-sacred birds but not to consecrated ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שִׁילּוּחַ הַקֵּן נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שילוח הקן applies everywhere and at all times, to חולין but not to מוקדשין.

steps.title: Covering the blood applies more widely than sending the bird
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares the two מצוות. כסוי הדם covers more cases than שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Covering the blood is stricter than sending away the mother bird. Covering the blood applies to wild animals and birds, to ones ready at hand and ones not ready at hand. Sending away the bird applies only to birds, and only to ones not ready at hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two ways that כסוי הדם reaches more cases than שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First difference: כסוי הדם covers both a חיה and a bird, while שילוח הקן covers only birds. Second difference: כסוי הדם applies whether or not the creature is מזומן, while שילוח הקן applies only when it is not מזומן. This sets up the next step, which defines 'not מזומן'.

keyTerms.meaning: A stricter point / something that applies more widely
Covering the blood after slaughtering a wild animal or bird
Ready at hand: already in one's possession and easy to take

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stricter' here does not mean a harsher punishment. It means the מצוה applies in more cases.

phrases.english: Covering the blood is stricter than sending away the bird,
for covering the blood applies to wild animals and to birds,
to those ready at hand and to those not ready at hand,

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁילּוּחַ הַקֵּן אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בָּעוֹף,
phrases.english: while sending away the bird applies only to birds,
and applies only to those not ready at hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more limits to the scope of שילוח הקן by comparing it to כסוי הדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שילוח הקן applies only to birds that are not מזומן. כסוי הדם applies to animals and birds, whether מזומן or not.

steps.title: What counts as 'not ready at hand'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines שאינו מזומן with examples: geese or chickens nesting in an orchard count, but birds nesting in the house, or house pigeons, are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'not ready at hand'? For example, geese and chickens that nested in an orchard. But if they nested in the house, and likewise house-raised pigeons, one is exempt from sending.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself what 'not ready at hand' means and answers with examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even tame birds like geese and chickens count as 'not ready at hand' when they nest out in an orchard, where they can fly off. If they nest inside the house, or are pigeons raised in the house, they are already in the owner's control, so there is no מצוה to send them away.

keyTerms.meaning: Pigeons raised in the house (domesticated pigeons)

phrases.english: What counts as not ready at hand?
For example, geese and chickens
that nested in the orchard.
But if they nested in the house,
and likewise domesticated pigeons —
one is exempt from sending away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'not מזומן' used in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds nesting outside, like in an orchard, are not מזומן and the מצוה applies. Birds nesting in the house, or house pigeons, are exempt.

steps.title: Non-kosher birds and mixed nests are exempt
steps.stepSummary: There is no מצוה with a non-kosher bird, and none when a kosher bird sits on non-kosher eggs or the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher bird: one is exempt from sending it. A non-kosher bird sitting on a kosher bird's eggs, or a kosher bird sitting on a non-kosher bird's eggs: one is exempt from sending.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more cases where there is no obligation of שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה applies only to a kosher mother sitting on kosher eggs. If either the mother or the eggs are from a non-kosher bird, the obligation does not apply.

phrases.english: A non-kosher bird — one is exempt from sending it away.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹף טָמֵא רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי עוֹף טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: A non-kosher bird sitting on the eggs of a kosher bird,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָהוֹר רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי עוֹף טָמֵא –
phrases.english: or a kosher bird sitting on the eggs of a non-kosher bird —
one is exempt from sending away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more exempt cases after the exemptions in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-kosher birds, and nests that mix kosher and non-kosher, are exempt from שילוח הקן.

steps.title: Dispute about a male bird sitting on the nest
steps.stepSummary: About a קורא זכר, a male bird that sits on the eggs, רבי אליעזר says one must send it away and חכמים say one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male קורא bird: רבי אליעזר obligates sending it, and the חכמים exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about whether the מצוה applies when the bird on the nest is a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The male קורא sits on the eggs the way a mother bird does. רבי אליעזר holds that one must still send it away. חכמים hold there is no obligation. The משנה does not give the reasons here.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of bird whose male sits on the eggs

steps.whatToRemember: שילוח הקן applies to kosher, non-sacred birds that are not מזומן, anywhere and at any time. There is a מחלוקת about a male bird on the nest.

phrases.english: A male korei bird —
רבי אליעזר deems one obligated,
and the Rabbis deem one exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹרֵא זָכָר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּיב וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed case after the agreed-upon exemptions in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Male קורא: רבי אליעזר says there is an obligation to send it away. חכמים say one is exempt.

steps.title: The phrase 'in the Land and outside the Land' is extra, except for the first shearing
steps.stepSummary: One of the two אמוראים says that whenever a משנה in our מסכת says a מצוה applies in ארץ ישראל and outside it, the phrase is not needed. The exception is ראשית הגז, where it rejects the view of רבי אלעאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי אבין and רבי מיישא disagree. One said: Anywhere we learned 'in the Land and outside the Land,' it was not needed, except for ראשית הגז. There it comes to reject רבי אלעאי, who said ראשית הגז applies only in the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a general rule about a phrase that keeps showing up in the משניות of this מסכת. One אמורא says this phrase usually adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these מצוות are tied to the person or the animal, not to the land, so it is obvious they apply everywhere. Only for ראשית הגז was there a real opinion, that of רבי אלעאי, limiting it to ארץ ישראל. So in that משנה the phrase does real work: it rejects his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Not needed; the phrase adds nothing new
The first of the shearing, the first wool given to a כהן
To exclude or reject (a certain view)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Avin and Rabbi Meyasha:
One said:
Anywhere that we learned in a משנה
"in the Land and outside the Land"
it is not needed,
except for the first of the shearing,
to exclude the view of Rabbi Ilai,
who said: "The first of the shearing
applies only in the Land."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי מְיָישָׁא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 4, which used the phrase 'בארץ ובחוצה לארץ'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בארץ ובחוצה לארץ' in our מסכת is not needed, except for ראשית הגז, where it rejects רבי אלעאי.

steps.title: The phrase 'with or without the Temple' is extra, except for an animal and its offspring
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says 'with or without the בית המקדש' is never needed, except for אותו ואת בנו. Since that law is written among the laws of sacrifices, one might think it applies only while sacrifices are brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: Anywhere we learned 'when the Temple stands and when it does not,' it was not needed, except for אותו ואת בנו. You might have thought: since it is written in the section about sacrifices, we keep it when there are sacrifices and not when there are none. So the משנה teaches us that it applies always.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives a parallel rule about a different phrase. He explains the one case where the phrase is really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These מצוות have nothing to do with the Temple, so normally it is obvious they apply after the חורבן. But אותו ואת בנו appears in the Torah among the laws of קדשים. So one could have wrongly tied it to times when sacrifices are offered, and the משנה had to rule that out.

keyTerms.meaning: While the בית המקדש is standing
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
It would enter your mind (a mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

phrases.english: And the other one said:
Anywhere that we learned
"when the Temple stands and when it does not stand"
it is not needed,
except for "it and its offspring."
It would enter your mind to say:
since it is written in the section about sacrifices,
at a time when there are sacrifices, we keep it;
at a time when there are no sacrifices, we do not keep it.
So it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same two-sided statement; a parallel rule about a different phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בפני הבית ושלא בפני הבית' is not needed, except for אותו ואת בנו, where one might have tied it to times when sacrifices are offered.

steps.title: Both agree 'with non-sacred and sacred animals' is needed, except for the sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: Both אמוראים say 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' is always needed, except for גיד הנשה. There it is obvious, since becoming holy would not remove the איסור of גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both of them said: Anywhere we learned 'with non-sacred and sacred animals,' it was needed, except for גיד הנשה. That is obvious! Just because an animal became holy, would the ban on גיד הנשה fall away from it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now both אמוראים agree on a third phrase. This time the phrase usually is needed, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the pattern is flipped: 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' normally teaches something real. For גיד הנשה, though, there is no reason to think holiness would cancel the ban, so the phrase seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as holy, for sacrifices
The sciatic nerve, which may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: The word פשיטא here is not the גמרא attacking anyone. It is part of the two אמוראים' own statement, explaining why the phrase is not needed for גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: And both of them said:
Anywhere that we learned
"with non-sacred and with sacred animals" — it is needed,
except for the sciatic nerve,
where it is obvious!
Just because it became holy,

phrases.aramaic: פְּקַע לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה מִינֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: would the ban on the sciatic nerve fall away from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third rule that both אמוראים share, following their two separate rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' is always needed, except for גיד הנשה, where it is obvious.

steps.title: Didn't we explain the sciatic nerve case as offspring of sacred animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the exception about גיד הנשה. Earlier, that משנה was explained as dealing with offspring of קדשים, which would make the phrase truly needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already explain that משנה as dealing with offspring of sacred animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last exception. It reminds us that the גיד הנשה משנה was already explained in a way that makes the phrase necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is about the young of a sacred animal, that animal was holy before its גיד הנשה even formed. Then one might think the ban on גיד הנשה cannot take hold, so the phrase would be teaching something real. That goes against the claim that it is 'obvious'.

keyTerms.meaning: We established, we explained the case as
The young born to sacred animals

phrases.english: But didn't we establish it
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה about גיד הנשה earlier in this מסכת (89b).

phrases.english: as dealing with the offspring of sacred animals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גיד הנשה exception in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' is obvious and not needed for גיד הנשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That משנה was already set up as dealing with ולדות קדשים. In that case one could think the earlier holiness blocks the ban on גיד הנשה, so the phrase is needed after all.

steps.title: The earlier explanation was only a fix for redundancy, and redundancy is not a real problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge about גיד הנשה. The explanation about offspring of קדשים was only made because the phrase looked unneeded. In truth, once the תנא listed needed phrases, he also listed an unneeded one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did we explain that משנה as talking about offspring of קדשים? Only because it bothered us that the phrase seemed unnecessary. But from the start that should not bother you: since the תנא taught phrases that were needed, he also taught one that was not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the claim that 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' is unneeded by גיד הנשה. It explains that the earlier explanation was never forced; it was just one way to solve a question that has an easier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, the challenge said the earlier explanation (offspring of קדשים) makes the phrase truly needed. The answer is that this explanation only existed to avoid saying the משנה wrote something extra. But the extra wording has a simpler reason. The משנה of אותו ואת בנו needed to say 'בחולין ובמוקדשין', and the גיד הנשה משנה repeated the same wording to match it, so Step 11's exception stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, along with; something was taught only because it came along with something else

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the explanation about offspring of קדשים was wrong. It is saying that explanation is not forced, so it cannot be used to prove the phrase is needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'אַיְּידֵי' idea is a common tool across ש״ס: a משנה can include an unneeded detail just because it sits in a list with needed ones.

phrases.english: And why did we establish it [that way]?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier explanation of the גיד הנשה משנה as talking about offspring of קדשים.

phrases.english: Was it not because it was difficult for us:
"Let it not teach it"?
phrases.notes: In other words, the question was that the phrase seemed obvious, so why write it at all?

phrases.english: From the start too, it should not be difficult for you;
since it taught [this phrase] where it was needed,
phrases.notes: The phrase was needed in the משנה about אותו ואת בנו, so the גיד הנשה משנה uses the same wording.

phrases.english: it also taught [it] where it was not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 and protects the exception stated in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undermines the basis of the challenge by showing the earlier explanation was not forced
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' by גיד הנשה must be needed, since we explained it as talking about offspring of קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: That explanation was only a fix for redundancy. Redundancy is acceptable because of אַיְּידֵי, so the phrase can be unneeded.

steps.title: Why the mother-bird מצוה does not apply to sacrificial birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which says שילוח הקן applies to חולין but not to מוקדשים, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the מצוה applies to non-sacred birds, but not to sacrificial ones. Why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from our משנה and asking for its source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא discussed whether phrases like 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' are needed. Here the משנה gives a real rule: the מצוה does not apply to מוקדשים at all. The גמרא wants to know where this exemption comes from.

phrases.english: "To non-sacred birds, but not to sacrificial ones."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about sending away the mother bird.

phrases.english: Why not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחוּלִּין אֲבָל לֹא בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁים אַמַּאי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion about needed phrases to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for exempting sacrificial birds from שילוח הקן.

steps.title: The verse limits the מצוה to a bird you are commanded to send away
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'שלח תשלח את האם' teaches that the מצוה applies only to a bird you are commanded to send away. A sacrificial bird is excluded because it must be brought to the גזבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'You shall surely send away the mother.' That means a bird you are commanded to send away. This excludes a sacrificial bird, which you are not commanded to send away; you must bring it to the Temple treasurer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14 with a דרשה on the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה is to send the mother away. That only makes sense for a bird you are free to let go. A bird belonging to the בית המקדש must be handed to the גזבר, so the מצוה of sending it away never applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall surely send away, the command of שילוח הקן

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a general rule: the מצוה only applies where sending away is something you are actually commanded to do. רבינא builds on this right away.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק limits the מצוה to a bird one is commanded to send away. A sacrificial bird must go to the גזבר.

steps.title: A kosher bird that killed a person is also exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבינא applies the same reasoning: a kosher bird that killed a person is exempt from שילוח, because it must be brought to בית דין, not sent away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, a kosher bird that killed a person is exempt from being sent away. Why? The פסוק says, 'You shall surely send away the mother,' meaning a bird you are commanded to send away. This excludes this bird, which you are not commanded to send away; you must bring it to court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא takes the rule from Step 15 and applies it to a new case: a bird that killed a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a sacrificial bird must go to the גזבר, a bird that killed a person must be brought to בית דין. Either way, you are not commanded to send it away, so the מצוה does not apply. The word 'הלכך' (therefore) shows that רבינא is building directly on the דרשה just taught.

steps.title: What case is רבינא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case of רבינא's ruling and starts with the first option: its verdict was already given.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances? If its verdict was already decided...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question about רבינא's case, starting to list possible situations. This line only begins the first option; the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know at what stage this bird is found sitting on its eggs. It starts with the case where בית דין already gave the verdict, and it will go on to test whether that case works.
